# Kratos continuum Gauss-point reference

Verified from the local Kratos checkout on 2026-11-04.

All indices are zero-based Python indices. GP number = index + 1. Coordinates are local (xi, eta, zeta); zeta is stored as 0 for 2D.

Plane stress and plane strain use the same geometry quadrature. Element interpolation order and integration rule are separate choices.

Scope: the 16 standard continuum geometries below, with all GI_GAUSS_1 to GI_GAUSS_5 geometry rules. Specialized element-owned rules, Lobatto/collocation rules, shells, beams and axisymmetric elements are outside this catalogue.

## Element types and defaults

Each rule table later in this document applies to every element listed with its corresponding geometry family. The listed default is used by ordinary geometry-based solids unless overridden.

| Example registered element | Geometry | Interpolation order | Default rule | GP count | Center Python index |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D3N` | Triangle2D3 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_1` | 1 | `0` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D6N` | Triangle2D6 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 3 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D10N` | Triangle2D10 | 3 | `GI_GAUSS_4` | 6 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D15N` | Triangle2D15 | 4 | `GI_GAUSS_5` | 12 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D4N` | Quadrilateral2D4 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 4 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D8N` | Quadrilateral2D8 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_3` | 9 | `4` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement2D9N` | Quadrilateral2D9 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_3` | 9 | `4` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D4N` | Tetrahedra3D4 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_1` | 1 | `0` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D10N` | Tetrahedra3D10 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 4 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D8N` | Hexahedra3D8 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 8 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D20N` | Hexahedra3D20 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_3` | 27 | `13` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D27N` | Hexahedra3D27 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_3` | 27 | `13` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D6N` | Prism3D6 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 6 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D15N` | Prism3D15 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_3` | 9 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D5N` | Pyramid3D5 | 1 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 5 | `None` |
| `SmallDisplacementElement3D13N` | Pyramid3D13 | 2 | `GI_GAUSS_2` | 5 | `None` |

## Definition of the center

The target is the reference-element area/volume centroid mapped through the geometry. The physical area/volume centroid of a distorted element can be different. `Geometry.Center()` can use a nodal average and should not be assumed to equal the mapped target for all orders/families.

| Family | Center local coordinates |
|---|---|
| triangle | (0.33333333333333331, 0.33333333333333331, 0) |
| quadrilateral | (0, 0, 0) |
| tetrahedron | (0.25, 0.25, 0.25) |
| hexahedron | (0, 0, 0) |
| prism | (0.33333333333333331, 0.33333333333333331, 0.5) |
| pyramid | (0, 0, -0.5) |

For pyramids, the reference volume centroid is (0,0,-0.5). If the desired target is instead local (0,0,0), none of GI_GAUSS_1 to GI_GAUSS_5 has a GP there. Pyramid weights are the raw Kratos weights, whose sum alone is not the reference pyramid volume because of the collapsed mapping.

## Active-rule center lookup

Each cell is `GP count / center Python index`; `None` means no GP at the target center.

| Family | GI_GAUSS_1 | GI_GAUSS_2 | GI_GAUSS_3 | GI_GAUSS_4 | GI_GAUSS_5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| triangle | 1 / 0 | 3 / None | 4 / 3 | 6 / None | 12 / None |
| quadrilateral | 1 / 0 | 4 / None | 9 / 4 | 16 / None | 25 / 12 |
| tetrahedron | 1 / 0 | 4 / None | 8 / None | 14 / None | 24 / None |
| hexahedron | 1 / 0 | 8 / None | 27 / 13 | 64 / None | 125 / 62 |
| prism | 3 / None | 6 / None | 9 / None | 12 / None | 15 / None |
| pyramid | 1 / 0 | 5 / None | 8 / None | 18 / None | 27 / None |

## Guidance for the consuming Python code

1. Identify a supported continuum geometry using local dimension and node count (or the geometry type/family). Never use node count alone to distinguish a 2D quadrilateral from a 3D tetrahedron or hexahedron.
2. Use `len(element.GetIntegrationPoints())` to obtain the active number of GPs. Within each family in this catalogue, the five counts are distinct, so family + count identifies the GI_GAUSS_n rule. Reject unmatched/custom rules. Do not infer the active rule solely from element order or the geometry default.
3. Read the family's rule record and its `center_index`. JSON `null` becomes Python `None`; index 0 is valid, so test `index is None`, not `if not index`.
4. `element.GetIntegrationPoints()` returns GLOBAL coordinates in active-rule order. It does not expose the local coordinates or weights in this catalogue. Map the chosen local center with `geometry.GlobalCoordinates(...)` before comparing it with those global GP positions.
5. Use the same index in the list returned by `element.CalculateOnIntegrationPoints(variable, process_info)`. Check the returned list length agrees with the active GP count.
6. If `center_index` is None, there is no central GP to select. A nearest GP or average is a different quantity.
7. Weights below are raw quadrature weights. Multiply by the appropriate Jacobian determinant and, for 2D volume measures, thickness. Negative weights in the triangle GI_GAUSS_3 rule are intentional.

## Ordered point-by-point rules

Rows preserve the exact source array order. Values below are binary64 evaluations of the expressions/constants stored in the checkout. Source SHA256 hashes are included in the matching JSON file.
